THREE genuine rendering bugs found and fixed during the mandatory manual read-back, none previously exercised by economics-12-1/12-2's own content shapes: (1) latex.py's _rewrite_divisions() operates on a whole $$...$$ block's text BEFORE a \begin{aligned} environment gets split into its own rows - on q_3.3's own two-row block ('M_T^D=KT \\& 1/K M_T^D=T'), the genuine division on row 2 searched backward for its numerator boundary straight through the row separator and found row 1's own trailing '=', swallowing row 1's right-hand side into a bogus fraction and leaving row 1 with an empty second line. Fixed by adding a depth-0 '\\' (row separator) and '&' (cell separator) as additional hard boundaries in both the numerator and denominator searches, same as the existing '=' check. Verified against a regression case (a normal single-row fraction with no \\/&) still renders correctly. (2) render_page_en.py's text_to_lines() sentence-splitter has no guard against a single-letter list marker ('a.', 'b.', ...) - this chapter's own solutions manual writes sub-lists this way (q_3.7, q_3.10), and every marker was being split onto its own stranded line, orphaned above its own list item. Fixed by not splitting when the accumulated buffer since the last split is exactly one lowercase letter plus a period. (3) The same splitter has no abbreviation guard at all - 'i.e.' split into two stranded fragments on q_3.7 ('...too i.' / 'e., the withdrawals...'), 'Rs.' (Rupees) split from its own following amount throughout q_3.10 and its own boxed answer, and 'Mr. B.' (q_3.10's own worked example) tore into four fragments. Fixed by protecting 'i.e.'/'e.g.' (with optional trailing comma), 'Rs.', and 'Mr.'/'Mrs.'/'Ms.'/'Dr.' (with an optional following single-capital-letter initial and its own period) the same way a $...$ math span already is, before line-splitting ever sees them.
